about: OpenEvidence is a Miami and Cambridge, Massachusetts-based medical AI company, founded in 2022 by Daniel Nadler, that offers a search and answer tool for clinicians using peer-reviewed literature, with content partnerships including NEJM and JAMA. It is widely used by US physicians, funded by advertising, and reportedly reached a valuation of about $12 billion in 2026 after raising roughly $1 billion in total. Strong brand among doctors but little with the general public.

Physical Intelligence is a San Francisco AI company, founded in 2024 by researchers including Karol Hausman, Sergey Levine and Chelsea Finn, that is developing foundation models for general-purpose robot control (the pi0 and pi0.5 models). It has raised about $1.07 billion from investors such as Thrive Capital, Lux and Bezos Expeditions, at a multi-billion valuation. Research-stage B2B company with little consumer awareness.

Prime Data Centers is a Newport Beach, California developer and operator of purpose-built, high-density data centers for hyperscalers and enterprises, with campuses in Los Angeles, Chicago and Virginia. The input shows reported funding of about $900 million. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Saviynt is a Los Angeles-area (Manhattan Beach) cybersecurity company, founded in 2010, providing a cloud-based identity security platform for identity governance, access management and privileged access, with AI features. Customers are large enterprises, government agencies and healthcare organisations. Backed by KKR, which led a $700 million investment in 2025, for a total of roughly $1.1 billion. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

Shengshu Technology is a Chinese AI company developing generative AI systems, best known for the Vidu text-to-video model. Founded in 2023 in Beijing and linked to Tsinghua University researchers, it has reported funding of about 6.5 billion yuan. Customers are creators and enterprises using its web service and API. B2B/prosumer, with limited consumer awareness outside China.

about: Socure is a New York-based identity verification and fraud prevention company, founded in 2012, that uses AI and data to verify digital identities, detect fraud and ensure compliance for banks, fintechs, telecoms and government agencies. It acquired Effectiv in 2024 and Qlarifi in 2025. Raised about $900 million, valued at around $4.5 billion. B2B, little consumer awareness.

V.tal is a Brazilian neutral digital infrastructure company, created in 2021 by BTG Pactual with Oi's fiber network, which offers wholesale fibre, backhaul and network services to telecom operators across Brazil. Based in Rio de Janeiro, it holds one of the biggest fibre networks in Latin America. Customers are operators like TIM, Claro and Vivo, and it reported over $1 billion in funding. B2B infrastructure, with little consumer brand awareness.

Waabi is a Toronto-based autonomous trucking technology company, founded in 2021 by Raquel Urtasun, a University of Toronto professor and former Uber ATG chief scientist. It builds the Waabi Driver using a generative AI simulator, working with Volvo Autonomous Solutions and Uber Freight. Funding is about $1.03 billion including a 2026 round. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

Xanadu is a Toronto-based quantum computing company, founded in 2016 by Christian Weedbrook, building photonic quantum computers (Aurora) and the PennyLane quantum software library. It serves researchers, enterprises and governments, and announced a plan to list through a SPAC merger with Crane Harbor in 2025. Funding about $986 million reported. B2B deep tech with limited consumer awareness.

XPENG Robotics is the humanoid robot and robotics business of Chinese EV maker XPENG (Guangzhou), developing robots such as the Iron humanoid. The input lists reported funding of about $1 billion. It is early-stage and tied to XPENG's AI strategy, so customers and revenue are not established. XPENG is listed on the NYSE and Hong Kong. Parent has strong consumer brand awareness in China and Europe.

about: Safaricom is Kenya's largest telecommunications company, based in Nairobi, offering mobile voice, data, fixed broadband and M-Pesa mobile money, with over 45 million customers in Kenya and Ethiopia (Safaricom Ethiopia). Majority owned by Vodacom (Vodafone) and the government of Kenya, and listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (SCOM). Extremely high consumer brand awareness in Kenya and a big sports and events sponsor.

Zuoyebang is a Beijing-based Chinese online education company, founded in 2015, behind a homework-help app and AI learning devices, tutoring and learning hardware for K-12 students. It has reached hundreds of millions of users and raised about $2.9 billion from investors including Alibaba, Tiger Global and SoftBank. Hit by China's 2021 tutoring crackdown. It is private. Strong consumer brand in China among parents and students.

Spotify is a Stockholm-based audio streaming company founded in 2006 by Daniel Ek and Martin Lorentzon, with more than 700 million monthly users and over 270 million premium subscribers in about 180 markets, offering music, podcasts and audiobooks. It earns subscriptions and advertising, with annual revenue around 15 billion euros. Listed on NYSE (SPOT). Extremely high consumer brand awareness, and a notable sponsor of football, including the Spotify Camp Nou for FC Barcelona and Wrapped campaigns.

Flipkart Marketplace is a subsidiary entity of Flipkart, the Bengaluru-based Indian e-commerce giant founded in 2007 by Sachin and Binny Bansal and majority-owned by Walmart since 2018. The marketplace entity lists third-party sellers for the Flipkart platform, the leading online shopping destination in India with hundreds of millions of customers, plus brands such as Myntra and PhonePe through related companies. Very high consumer brand awareness in India, with cricket and event sponsorships.

Animoca Brands is a Hong Kong-based digital entertainment and blockchain company, founded in 2014 by Yat Siu, with a large portfolio of Web3 gaming and metaverse investments (The Sandbox, Mocaverse, Axie Infinity, Moonbirds) and licensed games based on brands such as Formula E and MotoGP. It earns from games, investments and digital assets. Reported funding is about $843 million. Known in crypto and gaming circles, with modest mainstream consumer awareness.

Tekion is a San Ramon, California cloud-native software platform for automotive retail, founded in 2016 by Jay Vijayan (ex-Tesla), offering dealer management systems, CRM, finance and service tools with AI to car dealerships, OEMs and service shops. It has raised about $635 million at a valuation of about $4 billion. Customers are dealers and automakers across North America. B2B software, with low consumer brand awareness.

Life360 is a San Francisco-based family safety app and location-sharing company, founded in 2008, offering location sharing, crash detection and driving safety, and Tile trackers (acquired in 2021). It has over 90 million monthly active users in 150 countries and earns revenue from subscriptions and Tile products. Listed on Nasdaq (LIF) and the ASX. Strong consumer brand among families, especially in the US.

Triller is an American social video app, founded in 2015 and merged with TrillerVerz and AGBA in 2024, which lets users create AI-assisted music videos and hosts boxing and other live entertainment events (Triller Fight Club, BKFC). Based in Los Angeles, with a funding total of about $383 million. Listed publicly as Triller Group (Nasdaq: ILLR) after a SPAC with AGBA. Moderate consumer brand awareness, linked to combat sports.

about: Tempo is a US payments-first Layer 1 blockchain incubated by Stripe, built for stablecoin payments, with partners such as Visa, Deutsche Bank and Shopify. It raised $500 million in 2025 at a $5 billion valuation, led by Thrive Capital and Greenoaks. Customers are fintechs, banks and merchants. B2B infrastructure, mainly known in payments and crypto circles, with little consumer awareness.

Qihoo 360 Technology is a Beijing-based Chinese internet security company founded in 2005 by Zhou Hongyi, offering antivirus software, a browser, search and mobile security, and moving to AI and enterprise security. It was taken private from the NYSE in 2016 and relisted in Shanghai in 2018 (601360). Customers are hundreds of millions of Chinese internet users, with income from advertising and services. Strong brand in China, with very little profile abroad.

BT Group is the UK's largest fixed-line and broadband and mobile network operator, headquartered in London, with roughly 100,000 employees. Consumer brands include BT, EE and Plusnet; business unit BT Business and Openreach, the national access network, serve enterprises and wholesale customers. It also offers TV including sports channels such as TNT Sports (a joint venture, formerly BT Sport). Listed on the London Stock Exchange (BT.A) with annual revenue around 20 billion pounds. Very strong UK consumer brand with a history of sports sponsorship.

London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) is a global financial markets infrastructure and data company headquartered in London and listed on the LSE (LSEG). It operates the London Stock Exchange, LCH clearing, FTSE Russell indices and, since acquiring Refinitiv in 2021, the Workspace and Eikon data platforms, serving banks, asset managers and corporates worldwide with about 25,000 employees and revenue above 8 billion pounds. Microsoft holds a stake. B2B financial brand with high professional recognition.

Palantir Technologies is a US software company founded in 2003, listed on Nasdaq (PLTR) and long headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with the input showing a Miami base. Its Gotham, Foundry and AIP platforms integrate and analyse data for governments, defence and intelligence agencies and large enterprises across health, energy and industry. Revenue exceeds 3 billion dollars annually, growing with AI adoption. B2B brand with strong media and investor profile, and some F1 and commercial partnerships.

GoDaddy is a US internet services company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona and listed on the NYSE (GDDY). It is the world's largest domain registrar and sells web hosting, website builder, security, email and commerce tools to about 20 million customers, mostly small businesses and entrepreneurs, with revenue over 4 billion dollars. Founded 1997. Very high consumer awareness through heavy advertising, and a history of sports sponsorships including motorsport.

Harvey is a generative AI platform for legal and professional services firms, built to draft, review and research legal documents. Founded in 2022 and based in San Francisco, it is used by large law firms such as Allen & Overy (now A&O Shearman) and PwC, with backing from OpenAI Startup Fund, Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins and others, at a multi-billion dollar valuation. Customers are law firms and corporate legal departments paying enterprise subscriptions. B2B software with high profile in tech and legal circles but little mass-market awareness.

RLDatix is a healthcare software company providing patient safety, incident and risk management, governance, workforce scheduling and pharmacy compliance tools to hospitals and health systems worldwide. It was formed in 2020 by combining Reliance and Datix, and is headquartered in Chicago with large operations in Toronto and the UK. It is owned by private equity investors led by TA Associates. Revenue comes from software subscriptions. B2B brand with strong recognition among healthcare administrators but no consumer visibility.

Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) is a US pharmacy and retail healthcare group headquartered in Deerfield, Illinois, formerly listed on Nasdaq (WBA). Its Walgreens and Boots chains operate about 12,000 stores in the US, UK and Europe, alongside Alliance Healthcare wholesale and the VillageMD care business. Revenue is around 140 billion dollars, mostly pharmacy and retail sales. Founded 1901. Sycamore Partners took it private in a deal completed in 2025. Very high consumer visibility, with sports and community partnerships.

Wiz is a cloud security company founded in 2020 by Assaf Rappaport and colleagues, with US headquarters in New York and a large Israeli research base. Its agentless platform scans cloud environments such as AWS, Azure and Google Cloud for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and threats, and is used by many large enterprises. It raised well over 1 billion dollars at a valuation of about 12 billion dollars, and Alphabet agreed to acquire it for 32 billion dollars in 2025. B2B brand, widely known among security professionals but not consumers.

Zebra Technologies is a US enterprise technology company headquartered in Lincolnshire, Illinois and listed on Nasdaq (ZBRA). It makes barcode scanners and printers, RFID readers, mobile computers, tablets and machine vision, serving retail, logistics, healthcare and manufacturing customers worldwide with revenue around 5 billion dollars. Its Zebra MotionWorks tracking solution is used by the NFL to track players. Founded 1969. B2B technology brand, partly visible via sports data partnerships.

4Paradigm is a Beijing-based enterprise AI company founded in 2014 that sells machine learning platforms such as Sage, decision-intelligence software and large model tools to banks, retailers, manufacturers and governments. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2023. Revenue is around 5 billion yuan from platform and solution sales. B2B enterprise software with minimal consumer brand awareness.

Applied Intuition is a US software company based in Mountain View/Sunnyvale, California providing simulation, validation and vehicle operating system tools for automotive and defence autonomy customers, including many major automakers and the US military. Founded 2017 by former Waymo and Cruise engineers, it raised funding at a valuation of about 15 billion dollars in 2025 and also develops autonomous trucking and software-defined vehicle platforms. Revenue comes from software licences and services. B2B brand known in automotive engineering and defence technology.

Dataminr is a New York-based real-time event detection company founded in 2009 that uses AI to scan public data such as social media, news and sensor feeds and alerts corporate and public-sector clients to emerging risks. Customers include news organisations, governments, banks and large corporates, who pay for its alert subscriptions. It has raised hundreds of millions of dollars at a valuation of roughly 4 billion dollars. B2B brand with moderate profile in media, security and risk circles.

Deel is a global HR and payroll platform that helps companies hire, pay and manage employees and contractors in more than 150 countries. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Francisco, it reached a valuation of about 17 billion dollars in 2025, with annualised revenue reported above 1 billion dollars. Customers are businesses of all sizes; money comes from subscription and employer-of-record fees. B2B software brand with a strong tech-sector profile.

Didi Woya is a Beijing-based company developing autonomous driving technologies, according to its Crunchbase profile. It appears to be linked to the Didi ride-hailing ecosystem, but ownership, funding history, customers and scale are not confirmed from the input. B2B technology developer with little consumer awareness of its own. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Docusign is a US software company headquartered in San Francisco and listed on Nasdaq (DOCU) that pioneered electronic signature and now sells an Intelligent Agreement Management platform for preparing, signing, storing and analysing contracts. It has over a million business customers and revenue near 3 billion dollars from subscriptions. Founded 2003. Well-known B2B brand with a sizeable marketing budget.

Figma is a collaborative interface design tool used by product teams to design, prototype and share web and mobile apps in the browser, plus FigJam whiteboards and Dev Mode. Headquartered in San Francisco, it was founded in 2012 and listed on the NYSE (FIG) in 2025, after Adobe's 20 billion dollar bid was cancelled in 2023. Customers are designers and developers at companies of all sizes, paying subscriptions. Revenue is above 700 million dollars. Strong brand among creative and tech professionals.

Keysight Technologies is a US electronic design and test measurement company headquartered in Santa Rosa, California, spun out of Agilent in 2014 and listed on the NYSE (KEYS). It makes oscilloscopes, network analysers, 5G and 6G test systems and cybersecurity validation software for telecoms, automotive, aerospace and electronics customers, with about 15,000 employees and revenue around 5 billion dollars. B2B technology brand known to engineers.

KoBold Metals is a Berkeley, California mineral exploration company using AI and geoscience data to find critical minerals such as copper, nickel, cobalt and lithium for the battery industry. Founded 2018, backed by Bill Gates's Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz and Jeff Bezos, it holds a major copper project in Zambia (Mingomba) and explores in Canada, Australia and the US. Customers are mining and battery supply chain buyers. B2B startup with a strong investor profile, not a consumer brand.

Mavenir is a US telecom software company based in Richardson, Texas that builds cloud-native and Open RAN network software for mobile operators, including 5G core, voice, messaging and radio, with customers such as Vodafone, Orange and Dish. Owned by Siris Capital since a 2017 take-private, it did a major debt restructuring in 2025. Founded 2005. Revenue is licences and services. B2B telecom supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Megvii is a Beijing-based computer vision and AI company founded in 2011, known for its Face++ face recognition platform and for smart city, logistics and consumer device solutions. Customers include Chinese governments, banks and device makers. Investors included Alibaba and Ant Group. It was placed on the US Entity List in 2019 and its IPO plans stalled; it has leaned into logistics robotics and IoT. B2B AI company with little consumer awareness.

Momenta is a Chinese autonomous driving software company headquartered in Suzhou with offices in Beijing, Shanghai and Munich, founded in 2016. It develops driver-assistance and robotaxi software, supplying automakers such as SAIC and Toyota, and has run robotaxi trials in Shanghai and Germany. Investors include SAIC, Toyota, Mercedes-Benz and Tencent. It has explored a public listing. B2B automotive technology brand with little consumer awareness.

Perplexity is an AI-powered answer engine and search company founded in 2022 and based in San Francisco, which retrieves web results and generates cited answers, with Pro subscriptions, the Comet browser and an API. It serves tens of millions of monthly users and has raised funding at valuations reported near 20 billion dollars from investors including Nvidia and SoftBank. Revenue comes from subscriptions and enterprise plans. Strong tech consumer brand with fast-growing awareness.

Pony.ai is an autonomous driving company founded in 2016, with a base in Fremont, California and operations in Guangzhou and Beijing. It runs robotaxi services in Chinese cities and has tested in the US and Europe, partnering with Toyota, Uber and Chinese automakers; the company is listed on Nasdaq (PONY) and Hong Kong. Customers are ride-hailing users and fleet partners; revenue includes robotaxi fares and trucking pilots. Known in tech and mobility sectors, with a small consumer profile.

Revvity is a US life sciences and diagnostics company headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts and listed on the NYSE (RVTY), the former PerkinElmer after it sold its analytical and services units in 2023. It makes diagnostics, reagents, immunoassays, imaging and software for drug discovery, newborn screening and clinical labs, with revenue near 2.8 billion dollars. Customers are biopharma, hospitals and research institutions. B2B healthcare company with little consumer awareness.

Superhuman, formerly Grammarly, is a US AI-powered productivity company headquartered in San Francisco, which merged its Grammarly writing assistant with the Superhuman email client and Coda in 2025 under the Superhuman name. Grammarly's tools reach tens of millions of daily users, and it has raised large funding rounds including a 1 billion dollar financing from General Catalyst in 2025. Customers are individuals and businesses buying subscriptions. Very strong consumer awareness through heavy digital advertising.

Chainguard is a US software supply chain security company based in Kirkland, Washington that sells minimal, hardened container images, libraries and tools, built on its own Wolfi Linux distribution, to enterprises and developers. Founded 2021 by former Google engineers, it has raised funding at a valuation of several billion dollars from venture investors. Revenue comes from subscriptions. B2B developer brand known in cloud security communities but not to consumers.

Cohesity is a US data security and management company headquartered in San Jose/Santa Clara, California, selling backup, recovery, ransomware protection and AI-based data insight on its platform. It combined with Veritas's enterprise data protection business in 2024. Customers are enterprises and governments globally. Founded 2013 by Mohit Aron, with investors including SoftBank and Sequoia. Revenue is in the order of 1.5 billion dollars. B2B technology brand known to IT professionals.

Commvault is a US data protection and cyber resilience software company headquartered in Tinton Falls, New Jersey and listed on Nasdaq (CVLT). It sells backup, recovery, cloud data management and ransomware recovery to enterprises and governments, delivered as software and SaaS (Metallic), with revenue near 1 billion dollars. Founded in 1996 as a spin-off from Bell Labs. Customers are IT departments in over 100 countries. B2B brand, known to IT professionals.

Cybereason is a cybersecurity company offering endpoint detection and response, extended detection and response and managed threat hunting through its AI-driven platform. Headquartered in Boston with an Israeli research base in Tel Aviv, it was founded in 2012 and is backed by SoftBank and Liberty Strategic Capital; it merged with Trustwave in 2025. Customers are enterprises and managed service providers. B2B security brand with limited consumer awareness.

Gen Digital is a US consumer cyber safety company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona and listed on Nasdaq (GEN), formed in 2022 by the merger of NortonLifeLock and Avast. Its brands include Norton, Avast, AVG, LifeLock, Avira, CCleaner and MoneyLion, protecting hundreds of millions of users with antivirus, VPN, identity protection and financial tools, with revenue near 3.9 billion dollars. Descended from Symantec, founded 1982. Very high consumer awareness through direct marketing.

Heartflow is a medical technology company based in Mountain View/San Francisco, California that uses AI to create 3D models of coronary arteries from CT scans, helping cardiologists diagnose heart disease without invasive tests. Its Heartflow FFRct Analysis and plaque analysis are used in thousands of hospitals globally. Founded 2007 and listed on Nasdaq (HTFL) in 2025. Customers are hospitals and doctors, and revenue comes from per-analysis fees. B2B healthcare brand with little consumer awareness.

HyperVault AI Data Center is an Indian AI data centre business based in Mumbai that, according to its Crunchbase profile, enables hosting and compute for multiple AI workloads. Transdev is a French international operator of public transport, headquartered in Issy-les-Moulineaux and owned by Caisse des Depots (66 percent) and Rethmann. Customers are transport authorities and passengers. Formed 2011 by merger of Veolia Transport and Transdev. Visible brand on local buses and trains, mostly B2G.

Uniphore is a US enterprise AI company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with major development in Chennai, India, founded in 2008. It sells conversational AI, speech analytics and agentic automation for contact centres and customer service teams, through the Business AI Cloud platform, and acquired Emotion Research Lab, Jacada and Orby. It raised funds at a roughly 2.5 billion dollar valuation, backed by Nvidia, Snowflake and AMD. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Upland Software is a US cloud software company headquartered in Austin, Texas and listed on Nasdaq (UPLD). It has built a portfolio of enterprise work management and customer engagement products, such as Kapost, Altify, Qvidian, Mobile Commons and Waterfall, largely by acquiring smaller vendors. Customers are mid-sized and large organisations buying subscriptions, and revenue is around 300 million dollars. Founded 2010. B2B software with low consumer awareness.

Weimob is a Chinese cloud-based commerce and marketing software provider based in Shanghai and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (2013.HK). It sells SaaS tools and services that help merchants build online stores and run customer relationship and advertising campaigns inside the WeChat ecosystem, including retail, ecommerce and AI marketing products. Customers are retailers and brands, and revenue comes from subscriptions and marketing services. Founded 2013. B2B with little consumer awareness.

DigiPowerX is a Houston-based digital infrastructure company listed on Nasdaq (DGXX) that began in bitcoin mining and has shifted towards AI cloud and high-performance computing services, building data centres with GPU capacity. Swvl is a mass-transit mobility company headquartered in Dubai, offering an app for booking seats on shared, fixed-route buses and private rides, originally from Cairo with presence in Egypt, Pakistan, Kenya and more. about: Oura is a Finnish health technology company based in Oulu that makes the Oura Ring, a smart ring that tracks sleep, activity, heart rate and readiness, paired with a membership app. It has sold millions of rings, raising funds at a valuation reported near 11 billion dollars in 2025 with investors such as Fidelity and Dexcom, and has deals with the US military and retailers. Founded 2013. Strong lifestyle wearable brand with celebrity endorsements and sports and wellness partnerships.

Lovable is a Swedish AI software startup based in Stockholm, founded in 2023, whose platform lets users build web apps and websites by describing them in natural language, aimed at non-programmers and developers. It grew to tens of millions of dollars of annual revenue very quickly and raised funding at a valuation of several billion dollars from investors such as Accel and Creandum. Customers are individuals, startups and companies paying subscriptions. High-profile tech brand in the AI start-up scene.

Neko Health is a Swedish health-tech company based in Stockholm, co-founded in 2018 by Spotify's Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne, offering full-body scans with sensors and AI that give consumers a preventive health check in about 20 minutes at clinics in Stockholm and London. It raised funding at a valuation of about 1.8 billion dollars, led by Lightspeed and Atomico. Customers are self-paying consumers. Growing premium health brand with strong media coverage.

Abridge is a US healthcare AI company based in San Francisco that creates ambient AI clinical documentation, listening to doctor-patient conversations and generating notes for the electronic health record. Coalition is a US cyber insurance and security company headquartered in San Francisco that offers cyber insurance policies in the US, Canada and UK, combined with active scanning and monitoring tools.
